title: capsella bursa-pastoris coronopus
intro: Capsella bursa-pastoris coronopus, commonly known as shepherd's purse, is a flowering plant in the mustard family (Brassicaceae) that is often found growing in fields, along roadsides, and in other disturbed areas. The plant is used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory and antiseptic properties, which can aid in wound healing and reduce menstrual cramps. The therapeutic actions of shepherd's purse include its ability to reduce bleeding, lower blood pressure, and exhibit antioxidant and antimicrobial activities. The bioactive constituents of shepherd's purse include flavonoids, alkaloids, and saponins, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
